study type: Cross-sectional survey and pre/during epidemic administrative data analysis
outcome: medical procedures (e.g., Cesarean sections, laparotomy, open fractures, appendectomy, inguinal hernia)
cohort: The study included 3,631 households from Ebola-affected and non-affected health zones in North Kivu province, and administrative data from 56 health facilities in Ebola zones.
finding: The Ebola epidemic did not have large effects on general health system utilization or health outcomes, aside from Ebola virus disease itself, suggesting successful maintenance of health system capacity.
mod_finding: No significant difference in monthly mean Cesarean sections per facility was found when comparing the period before the Ebola epidemic to during the epidemic.
